headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Roo Code’s browser/MCP surface increases blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes project files in a plan-local sandbox, while Roo Code operates on VS Code workspace files and can use MCP. Because both can touch shared files and Roo Code may ingest file content or MCP outputs, attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent to the other. This is plausible in default setups, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or copied files are re-read by the other agent
IF Roo Code is configured to trust file or MCP content as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Disable MCP for the shared workspace
Require manual review before applying any file-derived instructions
Use a read-only handoff file between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write workspace files, and both can send context to model providers. Plandex explicitly handles model provider API keys, while Roo Code can call any configured OpenAI-compatible API and MCP servers. If sensitive source code or secrets enter the shared workspace, either agent can forward them to external services in default workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent is configured to send file contents to its model backend or an MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP servers for sensitive projects
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and broad network egress. Plandex shares state via a Plandex server backend, while Roo Code shares state via the filesystem. That creates a realistic write-conflict path on the same project tree, and Roo Code’s browser/MCP capabilities widen the set of mutable resources. Defaults are dangerous because concurrent edits can clobber each other.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace
IF either agent auto-applies edits while the other is active
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Turn off auto-apply on both agents
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply semantics, but Roo Code can act in multiple modes and has browser/MCP access. If Roo Code consumes Plandex output as authoritative, it may execute or render incorrect plans into code changes or external actions. The pair therefore has a strong default pathway from generated output to downstream action with limited verification.
conditions: IF Roo Code treats Plandex plans, diffs, or summaries as authoritative
IF Roo Code is allowed to take browser or MCP actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Require Roo Code to verify Plandex outputs against source files
Keep browser and MCP actions manual-only
Ask Plandex to emit machine-checkable diffs
Review every cross-agent handoff before execution
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or GDPR restrictions, so no direct compliance breach is evidenced. The main compliance risk is operational: both handle source code and API keys, and Roo Code can use browser/MCP surfaces that may log data externally. This is a documented-gap risk rather than a proven policy mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into either agent’s workspace
IF external model providers or MCP servers retain logs beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workspaces
Review provider retention settings before use
Disable browser capture on regulated projects
Use separate API keys per project
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy
